Article Title: BJP's Hardeep Singh Puri resigns as Rajya Sabha member from Uttar Pradesh
Article Text:
Rajya Sabha Chairman accepts Hardeep Puri's resignation from UP seat after MP bypoll win

NEW DELHI: Senior BJP leader Hardeep Singh Puri on Saturday resigned from his Rajya Sabha seat representing Uttar Pradesh , days after being elected unopposed to the Upper House from Madhya Pradesh.According to a bulletin issued by the Rajya Sabha, Puri's resignation has been accepted by the chairman with effect from November 14.The bulletin stated, "Shri Hardeep Singh Puri, an elected Member of the Council of States (Rajya Sabha), representing the State of Uttar Pradesh, resigned his seat in the Rajya Sabha and his resignation has been accepted by the Chairman, Rajya Sabha w.e.f. 14th November, 2026."Puri was elected unopposed to the Rajya Sabha from Madhya Pradesh last week after the nomination papers of two other candidates were rejected, leaving him as the sole contender in the by-election.The Madhya Pradesh seat had fallen vacant following the resignation of former Union minister of state L Murugan .
Article Summary: Senior BJP leader Hardeep Singh Puri on Saturday resigned from his Rajya Sabha seat representing Uttar Pradesh. Puri's resignation has been accepted by the chairman with effect from November 14. He was elected unopposed to the Upper House from Madhya Pradesh last week.

Article Title: 'Don't fall into BJP's trap': Raj Thackeray alleges bid to divide Mumbai over Chhath Puja
Article Text:
Raj Thackeray alleges BJP of 'divide and rule'

NEW DELHI: Maharashtra Navnirman Sena supremo Raj Thackeray on Thursday accused the ruling Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) of using Chhath Puja to create social and cultural tensions in Mumbai, urging people not to fall in a "political trap."In a post on X, Thackeray alleged that the BJP was attempting to provoke a confrontation between Marathi and North Indian communities ahead of the upcoming Uttar Pradesh assembly elections. He claimed that the party and its social media network were circulating reels around Chhath Puja and what he termed cultural aggression to create discord in Maharashtra.Thackeray also referred to Bhojpuri songs being played at some railway stations in Mumbai, claiming that the MNS had intervened to stop the practice."However, the BJP appears to be disappointed that all these efforts have still not managed to create the kind of conflict it expects. And all this exercise is being undertaken with the upcoming Uttar Pradesh elections in mind," he said.Questioning the BJP's political strategy, the MNS chief said the party's think tank appeared to have run out of ideas and that its long-standing "divide and rule" formula would no longer help it win elections.He alleged that the BJP had repeatedly attempted to exploit religious and caste divisions for electoral gains, claiming that it sought to create Hindu-Muslim tensions ahead of Lok Sabha elections and caste-based divisions before state assembly polls."Whenever Lok Sabha elections approach, it tries to ignite Hindu-Muslim tensions. It brings Muslim women wearing burqas into playgrounds and gardens and attempts to scare people by saying, 'Look, look, now they have reached our playgrounds and gardens.' Of course, several videos of people wearing burqas to create an atmosphere of terror among Hindu women and men are already visible on social media," he said.Thackeray also cited the row surrounding Mumbai's Kabutarkhana, alleging that the BJP had attempted to fuel a Gujarati-versus-Marathi divide ahead of the Mumbai Municipal Corporation elections last year."I have said several times in my speeches that when the BJP realises it cannot win elections by showcasing its work, it creates conflict between two groups and wins elections on the bloodshed that follows," he said.He further alleged that the Election Commission played the decisive role in electoral victories, while communal and social conflicts were used by the BJP to explain its success.
Article Summary: Raj Thackeray accuses BJP of using Chhath Puja to create social and cultural tensions in Mumbai. MNS supremo urges people not to fall in a "political trap" He alleges that the BJP was attempting to provoke a confrontation between Marathi and North Indian communities.

Article Title: 1 stenographer, 4,500 cases: HC seeks explanation over delay in pronouncing order
Article Text:
Delhi High Court has directed its registry to seek explanations

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Delhi High Court has directed its registry to seek explanations from a trial court judge, the chief judicial magistrate (CJM) and the district judge concerned over the failure to pronounce an order that was pending since April 22, 2026.Taking note of the remarks in the trial court's order sheets, Justice Manmeet Pritam Singh Arora sought clarification on the staff shortage and backlog of over 4,500 cases, which were cited to explain the delay.The matter stems from a petition filed by Pradeep Bansal and others under Article 227 of the Constitution, seeking time-bound disposal of an application dated April 8, 2024. The application seeks vacation of an interim stay granted on Dec 1, 2023, in a domestic violence complaint pending before a judicial magistrate, first class, in north Delhi.Justice Arora noted that arguments on the application were completed on Jan 6, 2026, but the trial court was yet to pronounce its order. The matter has remained pending for pronouncement since April 22 and has been deferred four times, most recently on Oct 27.After examining the trial court's order sheets, the high court observed that they did not disclose any clear reason for the prolonged delay. What particularly caught the judge's attention, however, were repeated references to administrative constraints in the trial court's proceedings.One of the order sheets recorded: "This court is working with only one stenographer and having pendency of more than 4,500 cases."Noting that the remark appeared in the order sheet and was followed by similar observations in subsequent orders, Justice Arora sought an explanation from the CJM and the district judge on the circumstances in which these remarks were made. They have been asked to clarify the staffing situation and the extent of case pendency in that court.The trial judge, meanwhile, has been asked to explain why the order has not been pronounced when arguments were concluded in Jan. The registry has been directed to obtain reports from all three judicial authorities, covering both the reasons for the delay and the administrative constraints cited, two days before the next hearing on Dec 3.
Article Summary: Delhi High Court has directed its registry to seek explanations over the failure to pronounce an order that was pending since April 22, 2026. Justice Manmeet Pritam Singh Arora sought clarification on the staff shortage and backlog of over 4,500 cases, which were cited to explain the delay.

He once again challenged PM Modi to a face-to-face public debate, saying it would expose who was under the control of foreign powers and involved in anti-national activities."The Prime Minister is aware of this because he has my phone tapped," Rahul said in a video posted by the Congress on X.Rahul also shared another video on X later, accusing PM Modi of relying on a script and claiming that the pressure of facing him in a debate was getting to the Prime Minister."The stage is yours, the atmosphere is yours—yet you still needed a script. Article Title: 'Brahmins' have been consulted: Akhilesh says he will visit Ram Temple
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav on Friday indicated that he would visit the Ram Temple in Ayodhya next month, saying that a date had been finalised after consulting members of the Brahmin community and checking astrological calculations."As for the date, our Pawan Pandey has consulted with many members of the Brahmin community, examined the planets (nakshatras), and drawing upon knowledge of astronomy, has determined a specific date and time, taking into account the positions of the Sun and the Moon," Yadav told reporters in a tongue-in-cheek response.On November 7, former Ayodhya MLA Pawan Pandey had announced that Yadav would visit Ayodhya on December 12. He is expected to be accompanied by his wife, Dimple Yadav, who is also a Lok Sabha MP. The two are likely to visit the Ram Temple as well as the Hanumangarhi Temple.The proposed visit has added to the political exchanges between the ruling BJP and the Samajwadi Party in Uttar Pradesh. The BJP has repeatedly criticised Yadav for not visiting the Ram Temple, accusing him of pursuing "appeasement politics".Yadav, meanwhile, has accused the BJP and Sangh organisations of wrongdoing in connection with donations collected for the temple, using the phrase "chanda chori".The December visit would be Yadav's first to the Ram Temple since its inauguration in January 2024. He had visited Ayodhya in October 2026 to attend a religious katha but did not visit the temple.There has also been speculation that the SP chief is adopting a softer Hindutva approach to counter the BJP. The ruling party has repeatedly brought up the police firing on kar sevaks in Ayodhya in the 1990s, when the state was governed by Mulayam Singh Yadav , Akhilesh's father.Akhilesh had earlier said he would visit the Ram Temple after the completion of Kedareshwar Dham, a project initiated during his government's tenure in Etawah.Uttar Pradesh chief minister Yogi Adityanath said that those responsible for firing on Ram devotees and subjecting saints to a lathi-charge should apologise before visiting the temple.On Tuesday, state BJP chief Pankaj Chaudhary also questioned the proposed date and asked Yadav to visit the temple on December 6 instead of December 12."If this is not a new political ploy in the name of Lord Ram but genuine repentance, then visit the Ram temple on December 6, not 12," Chaudhary, who is also a Union minister, said in a post on X.December 6 marks the anniversary of the demolition of the Babri Masjid in Ayodhya in 1992 by kar sevaks led by the Vishwa Hindu Parishad (VHP). The Ram Temple now stands at the site.
Article Summary: Akhilesh Yadav indicated that he would visit the Ram Temple in Ayodhya next month. He said that a date had been finalised after consulting members of the Brahmin community and checking astrological calculations. The proposed visit has added to the political exchanges between the ruling BJP and the Samajwadi Party in Uttar Pradesh.

NEW DELHI: Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav on Friday targeted UP CM Yogi Adityanath over his claim that 1.27 crore "Hindu voters" had been deleted from the electoral rolls. He raised qyuestions over the authenticity of the claim saying, "How the Election Commission provided him this information remains a mystery"."How can the chief minister say that names of 1.27 crore Hindu voters have been deleted (from the electoral rolls)? How the Election Commission provided him this information remains a mystery," news agency PTI quoted him as saying.He further said that the statement was part of a conspiracy "to spread fear in society"."He has made the comment to rile up sentiments he can benefit from," Yadav said."The BJP is now planning to bring in individuals from Madhya Pradesh, Jharkhand, Chhattisgarh, Bihar, Himachal Pradesh, Uttarakhand, and other parts, and have them registered as voters in Uttar Pradesh," he added.The Samajwadi Party chief accused the BJP government and the Election Commission of being in cahoots, alleging that while the opposition has no information, the chief minister knows that 1.27 crore Hindu voters have been deleted from the rolls."When a voter arrives to cast their ballot, they will be turned away on the pretext that their name is missing from the list," he said.The Samajwadi Party on Thursday asked EC to issue a notice to Uttar Pradesh CM Yogi Adityanath over his claim that 1.27 crore Hindu voters' names were missing from the state's electoral rolls.In a memorandum submitted to Uttar Pradesh Chief Electoral Officer (CEO), party state president Shyamlal Pal accused the poll panel of adopting different standards for the ruling party and the opposition. He pointed out that the EC seeks affidavits from opposition leaders who flag alleged irregularities in voter lists but has not questioned Adityanath over his statement. The SP said the chief minister should also be asked to submit an affidavit to protect the commission's credibility.The party also referred to a notice issued by the EC to SP chief Akhilesh Yadav on October 27, 2022, after he alleged discrepancies in the electoral rolls following the Uttar Pradesh assembly elections that year. NEW DELHI: The Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke in another X post on Monday claimed that the local Deputy Commissioner of Police (DCP) in his hometown had “suddenly gone on leave” and that a new officer had been brought in to take charge.Dipke’s remarks came amid party's earlier claim that he and fellow CJP leaders Ashutosh Ranka and Saurav Dass could be arrested before October 10 under the National Security Act (NSA) or other provisions.AISA national president Neha Bora on Monday claimed that protesting journalists have been detained at the Delhi Cantonment Police Station.In a post on X, Neha said "Rosy and other protesting journalists are detained at Delhi Cantt PS. Article Title: PM Modi a dictator, says Revanth after visas denied for summit

HYDERABAD: Telangana chief minister A Revanth Reddy on Friday called Prime Minister Narendra Modi a “dictator who doesn’t like to be questioned on anything”. He attacked the PM after it emerged that the central govt had denied visas to 115 delegates from 70 countries who were expected to attend the ongoing Bharat Summit, jointly organised by the Telangana govt and the Samruddha Bharat Foundation.Revanth also accused Union ministers from Telangana G Kishan Reddy and Bandi Sanjay, BJP state president N Ramchander Rao and BRS working president K T Rama Rao of working against Telangana’s interests by attacking the summit. “I would not consider the two Union ministers sons of the soil,” he said.“The state govt wants to showcase Telangana’s development to foreign delegates, who are experts in various fields and some journalists and attract investments to the state,” the CM added. “The delegates would have become brand ambassadors of Telangana. But the ministry of external affairs and ministry of home affairs cancelled visas at the last minute.”The CM also took a dig at BJP and BRS opposing Congress leader Rahul Gandhi ’s participation in Bharat Summit on Saturday. “Rahul Gandhi is Leader of the Opposition. He is the son and grandson of former PMs and belongs to a family that sacrificed lives for the country.Why is the BJP insulting him?” he asked.Rahul is expected to launch Telangana’s gig workers’ policy at the event.Revanth also said that when Rajiv Gandhi was PM, he had sent then Leader of the Opposition Atal Behari Vajpayee to foreign countries to participate in summits on behalf of the country. “Opposing Modi and BJP is not opposing India. Will Modi lose elections if one journalist questions him?” he asked.“The PM can hold BRICS and Raisina Dialogue inviting all delegates, but Telangana govt cannot conduct a summit which is part of Invest Global Summit 2026,” he said.Criticising BJP and BRS leaders, Revanth said both parties were blindly opposing the Telangana govt’s initiatives and projects such as metro rail expansion, Regional Ring Road, Musi rejuvenation project and even the Thummidihatti project.He called Kishan Reddy ‘Ghulam of Gujarat’ who wanted to divert investments in Telangana to the PM’s home state of Gujarat. Kishan and Sanjay did not even attend the Global Summit curtain raiser in Delhi last month, but Union minister Piyush Goyal did, he said. “We have till time tomorrow. If Kishan Reddy is willing to participate in Bharat Summit, I request our deputy CM Bhatti Vikramarka garu to personally extend an invitation to him,” he said.On the expenditure for Bharat Summit, the CM said they had all accounts and that it did not cost Rs 1 lakh crore, like the Kaleshwaram lift irrigation project did.
Article Summary: A Revanth Reddy attacked the PM after it emerged that the central govt had denied visas to 115 delegates from 70 countries. He also accused Union ministers from Telangana G Kishan Reddy and Bandi Sanjay, BJP state president N Ramchander Rao and BRS working president K T Rama Rao of attacking the summit.

Article Title: 20 of 33 judge posts vacant in Orissa HC, BJD MP urges Centre to act
Article Text:

With 20 of the 33 sanctioned posts of judges in Orissa high court set to remain vacant following the retirement of chief justice Harish Tandon, BJD Rajya Sabha MP Sasmit Patra on Saturday urged Union law minister Arjun Ram Meghwal to facilitate appointments through a time-bound process.In a letter to Meghwal, Patra said the high court’s working strength would fall to 13 judges after Tandon’s retirement on Nov 15, leaving around 60.6% of its sanctioned posts vacant. He pointed out that the vacancy rate was substantially higher than the national high court vacancy rate of around 26%.Patra said that despite judges joining the high court through transfers in 2025, subsequent retirements and transfers had reduced its working strength from 20 judges in Dec 2025 to 13.He linked the vacancies to the mounting case burden, citing a Union govt reply in Parliament in Aug this year that put the number of pending cases in Orissa HC at 1,70,346. Of these, 38,936 have been pending for more than a decade.“Fresh judicial appointments would considerably strengthen the high court’s institutional capacity,” Patra wrote.“I would therefore respectfully request your consideration in facilitating the filling up of judicial vacancies in Orissa high court, in consultation with the appropriate constitutional authorities, through a coordinated and time-bound approach,” he added.
Article Summary: 20 of the 33 sanctioned posts of judges in Orissa high court set to remain vacant. BJD Rajya Sabha MP Sasmit Patra has urged Union law minister Arjun Ram Meghwal to facilitate appointments through a time-bound process. Patra said the high court’s working strength would fall to 13 judges after Tandon's retirement.

New Delhi: A Delhi court has directed a deputy commissioner of police to monitor the expeditious processing of sanction to prosecute Wing Commander Manorath Singh Sabharwal, who was arrested on allegations of sharing sensitive Indian Air Force (IAF) information with Pakistani intelligence operatives.Chief judicial magistrate (CJM) Mridul Gupta issued the directions after the prosecution informed it that the sanction under section 152 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), as required under section 217 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), and sanction for offences under the Official Secrets Act were still pending.“Let report as to the same be filed by DCP concerned under his signatures by the next date of hearing, considering the delay already caused in the present matter,” magistrate Gupta said. The matter is listed for Dec 5.Recently, a chargesheet was filed by police alleging that Sabharwal was found in contact with a Pakistani intelligence operative through a honeytrap between Jan and April 2026 and shared sensitive information concerning fighter aircraft deployment, military exercises and a confidential drone unit.He allegedly also installed malware or spyware in the mobile phones of five subordinate officers, potentially compromising sensitive data.The court direction came after the defence counsel opposed the prosecution’s submission, highlighting the considerable delay in obtaining the requisite sanctions.The counsel of the accused officer also questioned the necessity of obtaining a sanction under the Official Secrets Act. After hearing the submissions, the court directed that a report on the progress of the sanction process be filed by the next date of hearing.The court also ordered the issuing of production warrants against the accused for the next hearing and issued a show-cause notice to the jail superintendent over his non-production before the court on the day of proceedings.On Dec 5, the court is likely to take cognisance of the chargesheet, while directing that the accused be produced through video conferencing every 14 days.
Article Summary: Wing Commander Manorath Singh Sabharwal was arrested on allegations of sharing sensitive Indian Air Force information with Pakistani intelligence operatives. The court direction came after the defence counsel opposed the prosecution’s submission, highlighting the considerable delay in obtaining the requisite sanctions.

Article Title: Not every insult attracts sec 299 of BNS: HC quashes FIR over FB post
Article Text:
Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar

:

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines





The Aurangabad bench of the Bombay high ourt has quashed an FIR registered against social worker Mohammad Hisham Osmani over a Facebook post, holding that not every insult or objectionable statement necessarily attracts Section 299 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS).The court observed that section 299 applies only to an aggravated form of insult to religion or religious beliefs, accompanied by a deliberate and malicious intention to outrage the religious feelings of a particular class of citizens.Justice Sushil M. Ghodeswar passed the order on Nov 3, allowing Osmani’s criminal application seeking quashing of the FIR. The FIR was registered at Pundaliknagar police station on Feb 21, 2026, under section 299 of the BNS, which carries a punishment of up to three years’ imprisonment, a fine, or both.Osmani, a former city president of the Congress party, had resigned from the party in protest against the renaming of Aurangabad as Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar.The FIR was lodged by Ashok More Patil for an offence said to have occurred between Feb 19 and 21. The FIR mentions that on the evening of Feb 19, a cultural programme was held in Agra, Uttar Pradesh, on the occasion of Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Jayanti and telecast live on television.More alleged that on Feb 21, he saw a Facebook profile in the applicant's name on his mobile phone and found a post carrying sarcastic remarks in Hindi, using metaphors of donkeys and mujra against certain persons and their boss. He claimed it hurt his religious feelings.The HC had allowed a connected application filed by Vinod Narayan Patil as an intervenor. While representing Osmani, Adv SS Kazi submitted before the HC that the police registered the FIR without any inquiry and without calling Osmani, and also that he was unaware of it.Kazi submitted that after an objection was received over the post, a police officer asked Osmani to delete it at around 10 pm on Feb 21, about four hours after the FIR was registered, and that he deleted it immediately.Kazi, appearing for the applicant, read out section 299 and argued that no offence under it was made out. Assistant public prosecutor for the state and complainant’s advocate opposed the petition, submitting that the investigation was almost complete and the charge sheet was being prepared.Witness statements showed that the post was found on the Facebook account maintained by the applicant.After going through the FIR and the statements recorded by the investigating officer, the high court said that even if the post was taken at face value, it did not disclose any specific insult to the religion or religious beliefs of any particular class of citizens.“Mere use of insulting or abusive expressions against certain persons, without satisfying the aforesaid essential ingredients, would not constitute an offence under section 299,” it observed.The HC concluded that to prevent abuse of the process of the court and secure the ends of justice, it quashed the FIR and consequential proceedings, if any, to the extent of the applicant.
Article Summary: Aurangabad bench of the Bombay high ourt has quashed an FIR registered against social worker Mohammad Hisham Osmani over a Facebook post. The FIR was lodged by Ashok More Patil for an offence said to have occurred between Feb 19 and 21.

Article Title: BJP, Shiv Sena and NCP locked in tug-of-war for Satara DCC bank chief’s post
Article Text:
Satara DCC Bank

Kolhapur:

Mahayuti parties — BJP Shiv Sena and NCP — are once again at loggerheads over the election of the chairperson of the Satara District Central Cooperative Bank, scheduled for Nov 18. Although all three parties are part of the ruling alliance, differences over the bank’s leadership have triggered a fresh political tug-of-war.In the Sangli DCC chairperson election, the Maha Vikas Aghadi has a majority of 11 directors out of 21 on its side. It is now looking to rope in Shiv Sena, which has won three seats in the Sangli DCC, into its arrangement to keep the BJP from inching closer to power.In Satara, the BJP has nine directors, the NCP eight and Shiv Sena four. The 21-member board will elect the chairperson, with the majority mark fixed at 11 in the Satara DCC as well.The contest carries the baggage of a bitter recent past. When the Shiv Sena and NCP combine had a majority to elect the Zilla Parishad president, the BJP managed to win over turncoats from the two parties and ensured its candidate’s victory.Ministers Shamburaj Desai of Shiv Sena and Makarand Patil of the NCP had alleged that they were assaulted by police during the Zilla Parishad president election.Amid this, chief minister Devendra Fadnavis has deployed minister Shivendraraje Bhosale to find a solution and get all three parties together.NCP and Sena are eager to take revenge against BJP, but the extent to which they will succeed is crucial.“I have been asked by the CM to get all local leaders of Mahayuti to sit together and find a way out and if it is not possible then the CM can intervene,” said Bhosale.Bhosale on Thursday night met deputy CM Eknath Shinde at the latter’s Dare Tam house. They both discussed the political situation in Satara DCC. According to sources, Sena and NCP are likely to pitch for their chairperson for the DCC.In Sangli, Sena is moving closer to MVA parties and may secure the vice-chairperson’s post if its three directors support the MVA candidate, sources said. Congress, which has six directors in MVA, may get the first opportunity to elect the chairperson from among its directors.
Article Summary: Mahayuti parties are at loggerheads over the election of the chairperson of the Satara District Central Cooperative Bank, scheduled for Nov 18. All three parties are part of the ruling alliance, but differences over the bank’s leadership have triggered a fresh political tug-of-war. Maha Vikas Aghadi has a majority of 11 directors out of 21 on its side.

Article Title: 4 govt directors help BJP-led group win Kolhapur's Gokul polls; another form of vote and election chori, says Congress
Article Text:
Maharashtra’s BJP-led Mahayuti alliance secured victory in the Gokul Dairy chief election held recently





KOLHAPUR: Maharashtra ’s governing BJP-led Mahayuti alliance snatched Tuesday a win over Congress-backed group Samavichari Aghadi in a high-stakes election for Kolhapur-based Gokul Dairy’s chief, riding on the support of four new govt nominees.Mahayuti candidate, ex-NCP MLA Rajesh Patil, was elected chief after securing 16 votes, three more than his Samavichari rival Patil Chuyekar’s 13.Gokul has a 25-member board of directors, for which elections were held last month. Mahayuti had won 12 posts and Samavichari 13. Neither had the quorum of 14 required for the chief’s election.Mahayuti govt had last week promulgated an ordinance to nominate five members to large cooperatives, four with voting rights.This drew flak from the opposition, which accused govt of attempting to grab Gokul, the state’s largest milk co-operative. Congress LS leader of opposition Rahul Gandhi alleged “adulteration” of the mandate. A Samavichari plea in Bombay HC against the ordinance was rejected Monday.“We have nominated individuals with experience. If one is a gynaecologist, what’s wrong? When the country’s leader of opposition feels the need to intervene in a milk union election, a gynaecologist is just a common citizen,” CM Devendra Fadnavis said on Tuesday.Congress general secretary KC Venugopal denounced the outcome as “another form of vote and election chori”.
Article Summary: BJP-led Mahayuti alliance snatched a win over Congress-backed group Samavichari Aghadi in a high-stakes election for Kolhapur-based Gokul Dairy’s chief. Rajesh Patil, ex-NCP MLA, was elected chief after securing 16 votes.

Article Title: Rs 1 lakh bribe trap: Navi Mumbai ACB catches circle officer, talathi and woman assistant
Article Text:
The arrested accused were identified as Keshav Dagdu Mohite, Jaihind Birsha Koli (49) and Monika Vijnesh Patil (36).





NAVI MUMBAI: The Navi Mumbai Anti-Corruption Bureau (ACB) has arrested two revenue officials and a woman assistant for allegedly accepting a Rs 1 lakh bribe from a villager in Chirner, Uran taluka, to register the names of his relatives in the 7/12 extract of a land record.The arrested accused were identified as Keshav Dagdu Mohite (52), circle officer at Koproli in Uran taluka; Jaihind Birsha Koli (49), talathi; and Monika Vijnesh Patil (36), an assistant to the revenue officials.Dharmaraj Sonake, deputy superintendent of police, Navi Mumbai ACB, said the complainant had applied to register the names of the heirs of his deceased sister in the 7/12 extract of their land in Chirner.The land was jointly owned by the complainant's maternal uncle, aunt, brother and sister. The complainant had also applied for deletion of his deceased brother's name and submitted the request to circle officer Mohite and talathi Koli. However, the two officials allegedly demanded Rs 1 lakh from him to process the work.Dy SP Sonake said, "After verification of the complaint on Monday, when it was confirmed that the revenue officers Mohite and Koli had told the complainant to hand over the bribe amount to the accused woman assistant Monika Patil, a trap was laid on Tuesday around 2 pm. After the woman assistant Monika Patil accepted the demanded bribe of Rs 1 lakh from the complainant and handed it over to circle officer Keshav Mohite, both were caught red-handed and arrested. While, the acccused Talathi Jaihind Koli who was involved in the bribe demand was taken into custody from Dronagiri."
Article Summary: The Navi Mumbai Anti-Corruption Bureau (ACB) has arrested two revenue officials and a woman assistant for allegedly accepting a Rs 1 lakh bribe. The arrested accused were identified as Keshav Dagdu Mohite (52), circle officer at Koproli in Uran taluka; Jaihind Birsha Koli (49), talathi; and Monika Vijnesh Patil (36)

Rejection, and subsequent restoration, of Sumit Patil’s nomination has become the central flashpoint in the Jalgaon District Central Cooperative Bank election, scheduled for Nov 29.The decision has ended the prospect of an unopposed victory for BJP-backed candidate Satish Shinde in Pachora and sharpened tensions within the ruling Mahayuti alliance. Sumit is the son of Pachora Shiv Sena MLA Kishor Patil.A senior Shiv Sena functionary said that with Sumit back in the fray, the key BJP-backed candidate Satish Shinde’s prospects of an unopposed victory from Pachora have now been dashed.The Mahayuti alliance aims to contest unitedly, but seat-sharing friction has stalled a final agreement. At a meeting in Jalgaon attended by Girish Mahajan, Gulabrao Patil and NCP leaders, BJP demanded the largest share of nine seats. The deadlock continues over Muktainagar, Bhadgaon, Raver and Chopda, compounded by Kishor Patil’s absence from the meeting.The crisis began on Nov 3 when returning officer Manoj Chaudhary disqualified Sumit, prompting Kishor Patil to state that there are invisible forces working against his family.Sumit challenged the rejection before the divisional joint registrar of cooperatives in Nashik. The appellate authority overturned the returning officer’s order and declared his nomination valid, allowing him to re-enter the electoral contestWith over 300 candidates in the fray and none withdrawing, the contest intensified for the 21-member board of directors for the 2026-2031 term, comprising 15 taluka representatives and six reserved seats.Over 3,000 eligible voters make up the electoral roll. Heavyweights including Union minister Raksha Khadse, ministers Girish Mahajan and Gulabrao Patil, and MLA Mangesh Chavan entered the fray.A senior BJP member said the development underscored how North Maharashtra’s cooperative sector was losing its traditional grassroots ethos to aggressive party politics. Cooperative banks, rather than functioning as member-driven financial institutions focused on agricultural credit, had become high-stakes battlegrounds for political supremacy, dynastic succession and party dominance.Three seats were decided unopposed, reinforcing political dynasties. In Parola and Erandol, Nalini Patil, mother of MLA Amol Patil, and Mrunal Patil, Amol Patil’s wife, along with Rajani Savkare, wife of textile minister Sanjay Savkare in Bhusawal, secured unopposed victories.On the opposition front, the Maha Vikas Aghadi fielded an independent panel. Prominent contenders include Congress district president Avinash Bhalerao, Rajiv Patil, Uday Patil, NCP district president Pramod Patil, Kalpita Patil, Vaishali Patil, and Pradeep Deshmukh.Political circles are also watching coordination between the two NCP factions after local leaders appeared alongside Dr Satish Patil.
Article Summary: Sumit Patil's nomination has become the central flashpoint in the Jalgaon District Central Cooperative Bank election, scheduled for Nov 29. The decision has ended the prospect of an unopposed victory for BJP-backed candidate Satish Shinde in Pachora.

Article Text:
Sujay Vikhe (R) takes seat as chairperson of ADCC Bank alongwith Ranjitsinh Deshmukh as vice-chairperson. Former minister Balasaheb Thorat (extreme left), Ram Shinde, chairperson legislative council and WRD minister Radhakrishna Vikhe were also present

Former MP and BJP state vice-president Sujay Vikhe Patil was elected unopposed as chairperson of the Ahilyanagar District Central Cooperative Bank on Thursday, following a rare alliance between political rivals — guardian and water resources minister Radhakrishna Vikhe Patil and former revenue minister Balasaheb Thorat.Ranjitsinh Deshmukh was elected unopposed as vice-chairperson. Backed by 20 of the 21 directors, including independents and the Ram Shinde faction, Vikhe’s selection followed his panel’s victory in 17 of the 21 seats, out of which 10 were won unopposed. Playing a key coordinating role in bringing the opposing factions together, Vikhe Patil celebrated with supporters after taking charge.“We all will work with cohesion for the welfare of the bank, farmers and industries. We will function under the directions of senior leaders in the district and serve in the best interest of the bank’s owners i.e. the farmers,” Vikhe Patil told the reporters.On the eve of the election, Sangamner director Ranjitsinh Deshmukh met Lok Sabha MP Nilesh Lanke at Supa rest house, sparking speculation. Defending the alliance, Thorat said farmers’ welfare outweighed politics amid drought conditions.“The district bank belongs to the common man and must survive.Given the drought-like situation, we kept politics aside and came together to work for farmers,” Thorat said.Meanwhile, Lanke, the lone opposition director who skipped the election process and signed the attendance register after arriving late, vowed to act as a strict watchdog. Declining to comment on internal backing, he said that the majority holds the right to decide.“I am alone in the opposition in the bank. I am the chowkidaar (watchman). I will keep a strict vigil and discharge this duty honestly,” Lanke said, demanding large-scale crop loans at low interest rates. If only my farmer survives will the sugar industry survive,” he added.
Article Summary: Former MP and BJP state vice-president Sujay Vikhe Patil was elected unopposed as chairperson of the Ahilyanagar District Central Cooperative Bank on Thursday. He was backed by 20 of the 21 directors, including independents and the Ram Shinde faction. Former revenue minister Balasaheb Thorat was elected as vice- chairperson.

Cuddalore: Tension gripped Pudupettai near Panruti in Cuddalore district after a woman set herself ablaze inside the local police station premises following a dispute over her husband’s detention in connection with a clash over allocation of work under the rural employment scheme. The woman, identified as L Kanmani, sustained severe burn injuries and has been admitted to the Panruti Govt Hospital.Trouble erupted in Oraiyur village near Panruti between Kanmani, who serves as a worksite supervisor under the rural employment scheme, and panchayat clerk Arul over the allocation of work. Following an altercation, Kanmani lodged a complaint at the Pudupettai police station alleging that Arul had assaulted her, while Arul filed a counter-complaint accusing Kanmani and her husband, Latchathipathi, of attacking him.Police summoned both parties to the station for an inquiry. During the proceedings, police detained Latchathipathi over allegations of assaulting the panchayat clerk. Kanmani pleaded with the officers to release her husband, maintaining that he had not committed anything wrong. When her pleas went unheeded, she suddenly doused herself with petrol and set herself on fire inside the police station.Personnel at the station rushed to extinguish the flames and shifted the injured woman to the Panruti Govt Hospital. As news of the incident spread, Kanmani’s relatives gathered in large numbers outside the police station and staged a road blockade, demanding strict action against the police personnel involved.
Article Summary: Tension gripped Pudupettai near Panruti in Cuddalore district after a woman set herself ablaze inside the local police station premises. The woman, identified as L Kanmani, sustained severe burn injuries and has been admitted to the PanRuti Govt Hospital.

Article Text: KRISHNAGIRI: State industries minister S Keerthana participated in Children’s Day celebrations at the Government Higher Secondary School in Chinna Melupalli near Krishnagiri on Friday.The minister attended the celebrations as a special guest and paid floral tributes to a portrait of former Prime Minister Jawaharlal Nehru whose birth anniversary is celebrated as Children’s Day. Kerala High Court on Friday directed the state police chief to ensure that the Patriarch of Antioch, Ignatius Aphrem II, head of the Jacobite faction, does not violate the decrees and Supreme Court judgments governing the dispute between the Orthodox and Jacobite factions during his visit to Keralam from Syria as a state guest.Justice P V Kunhikrishnan issued the interim order on a petition filed by V V Mathew of Manarcadu and two others seeking a directive to the govt and police to ensure that the patriarch does not engage in religious activities, including celebrating Holy Qurbana at St Mary’s Church, Manarcadu, or at any other church belonging to the Malankara Orthodox Syrian Church. The police shall also ensure that the patriarch doesn’t violate his visa conditions. Additionally, taking note of the additional advocate general’s submission that subsequent HC judgments had also made certain clarification on the scope of the decrees, the court directed the state police chief to take those judgments into consideration as well and posted the petition to Nov 23.The Patriarch of Antioch arrived in Kerala on Nov 11 as a state guest and is scheduled to return on Nov 16. The petitioners sought to prevent the patriarch from conducting any religious activities, including celebrating Holy Qurbana, in violation of the decrees and the Supreme Court’s authoritative judgment in the K S Varghese case and other reported decisions.According to the petitioners, the SC had held that the patriarch could not interfere in the administration of parish churches by appointing vicars, priests, deacons or prelates in violation of the 1934 Constitution of the Malankara Orthodox Syrian Church (MOSC).The petitioners also pointed out that the patriarch, a Syrian citizen, had obtained an X-Miscellaneous Entry Visa to visit India. Under the terms of this visa, a foreign national cannot engage in preaching, proselytisation or organised religious or missionary programmes in India.During the hearing, the bench expressed its displeasure at the way in which the leaders of the Jacobite factions treated the special messenger who was sent by the court to serve notice in the petition. The special messenger reported to the court that while he reached the patriarch centre at Puthencruz to serve notice, certain office bearers allegedly threatened him that a case would be registered against him and asked him to return without serving the notice. Perusing the report, the court directed the HC registry to forward the complaint of the special messenger to the SHO of the jurisdictional police station.
Article Summary: The Kerala High Court on Friday directed the state police chief to ensure that the Patriarch of Antioch, Ignatius Aphrem II, does not violate the decrees and Supreme Court judgments. Justice P V Kunhikrishnan issued the interim order on a petition filed by V V Mathew of Manarcadu and two others.

Article Title: Introduce kidney-swap programme, streamline transplants: HC to govt
Article Text:
A division bench of Chief Justice Soumen Sen and Justice V M Syam Kumar issued the order on a petition filed by a 20-year-old from Thrissur seeking measures to prevent the commercialisation of organ donation.

Kerala High Court has directed govt to implement the recommendations of an advisory committee constituted in 2024 to reform organ transplantation in the state. Among other measures, the committee recommended setting up a digital platform to facilitate altruistic live organ donation and introducing a kidney-swap programme.A division bench of Chief Justice Soumen Sen and Justice V M Syam Kumar issued the order on a petition filed by a 20-year-old from Thrissur seeking measures to prevent the commercialisation of organ donation. The petitioner’s father had died of kidney disease at 46 after struggling for four years to secure a transplant.The advisory committee submitted its report to govt following a meeting on Nov 19, 2025, recommending several measures to promote altruistic organ donation. It suggested that K-SOTTO (Kerala State Organ and Tissue Transplant Organisation), in consultation with National Organ and Tissue Transplant Organisation (NOTTO), set up a digital platform to facilitate non-directed altruistic donation of organs and tissues, including kidneys, portions of the liver and skin, to needy patients.The committee recommended that K-SOTTO alone invite applications to ensure strict confidentiality and anonymity.The organisation would initially bear the costs of donor evaluation, which the recipient could reimburse after a successful transplant.The bench directed the state govt to introduce a kidney-swap programme, under which two or more families with incompatible living donors exchange donors to ensure that each patient receives an organ compatible with their blood group or tissue type. The programme must strictly comply with Section 9(3A) of the Transplantation of Human Organs and Tissues Act.The court also asked K-SOTTO to develop a platform to assess the number of patients with end-stage kidney, liver and heart diseases to help formulate long-term policies.Other recommendations of the committee included revamping the police inquiry into reports of illegal organ transplantation in Thrissur district, requiring transplant centres to disclose charges transparently, publishing upper limits on charges and introducing a single-window, time-bound clearance system for transplant approvals.Citing Supreme Court’s directions in Indian Society of Organ Transplantation v. Union of India, the bench said it was now the state’s responsibility to accept and implement the recommendations.
Article Summary: A division bench of Chief Justice Soumen Sen and Justice V M Syam Kumar issued the order on a petition filed by a 20-year-old from Thrissur. The petitioner’s father had died of kidney disease at 46 after struggling for four years to secure a transplant.
